title: Explore ClawSweeper-inspired GitHub maintainer automations for OpenHands
description: Evaluate patterns from openclaw/clawsweeper for OpenHands extensions and automations. ClawSweeper is not something to copy wholesale: it is OpenClaw- and Codex-specific, operationally heavy, and includes auto-close/automerge behavior that should not become an OpenHands default. The useful proposal is to mine it for architecture: marker-backed GitHub comments, maintainer-only command routing, durable structured run records, deterministic mutation executors, exact-head safety gates, lane/capacity limits, and opt-in bounded repair loops.
design: Treat ClawSweeper as a reference architecture, not a dependency. Prefer OpenHands Cloud Automations / plugins / SDK primitives over Codex-specific code. Keep write actions opt-in, permission-checked, and deterministically gated.
acceptance_criteria: A short design note or PRD exists that identifies which ClawSweeper patterns OpenHands should adopt, which to avoid, and a phased implementation plan for extension/plugin work.

title: Design marker-backed GitHub status comments for OpenHands automations
description: Define a comment contract for OpenHands GitHub automations that posts one durable status comment per issue/PR and edits it in place. Use hidden markers to identify the owning automation, target repo, issue/PR number, head SHA when applicable, intent, and conversation/run id. This addresses bot-comment spam and gives maintainers a stable status surface.
design: Inspired by ClawSweeper marker-backed comments. Keep prose concise and link to OpenHands conversation/run state. Do not rely on scraping visible prose; use hidden markers and structured local/backend records.
acceptance_criteria: Design covers marker format, idempotent lookup/update behavior, visible states such as queued/reviewing/fixing/done/blocked, stale-head behavior for PRs, and compatibility with GitHub issue comments and PR review comments.

title: Prototype maintainer-only @openhands GitHub command router
description: Prototype a command router for GitHub issue/PR comments that recognizes maintainer commands like @openhands review, @openhands explain, @openhands fix ci, @openhands address review, and @openhands rebase. The router should verify author permissions before dispatching write-capable work and should ignore or politely reject unsafe commands from non-maintainers.
design: Use GitHub APIs/gh for permission checks. Treat issue/PR author permissions separately from maintainer permissions. Read-only commands can be broader; write actions require admin/maintain/write or explicit repo policy.
acceptance_criteria: Router design or prototype documents supported commands, permission checks, idempotency ledger, status-comment updates, and dispatch into OpenHands Cloud Automations or plugin workflows. Initial scope should be review/explain and maybe fix-ci; no auto-close or automerge by default.

title: Define durable run records for GitHub automation state
description: Define the structured record that OpenHands GitHub automations persist for each run. The record should make retries, audits, status comments, and dashboards possible without relying on conversation logs or GitHub comments as the only source of truth.
design: ClawSweeper uses a state repo; OpenHands may prefer the automation backend DB. Keep the schema backend-agnostic enough that a plugin can start with JSON artifacts and later move to managed storage.
acceptance_criteria: Schema proposal includes repo, item type/number, head SHA, command/intent, requester, permission decision, conversation id, status, findings summary, validation commands/results, created/updated timestamps, and links to artifacts/logs. Storage location is decided: automation backend DB, repo state file, or plugin-managed artifact.

title: Specify deterministic mutation executor boundaries for GitHub repair workflows
description: Design the safety boundary between an OpenHands agent conversation and deterministic GitHub mutation code. The agent may review, plan, edit, and validate. Deterministic code should own permission checks, allowed repository boundaries, exact-head checks, branch naming, push/PR creation, labels, comments, and any merge gate.
design: Use ClawSweeper's model as inspiration: agent decides what code needs to change; deterministic code decides whether and how mutations are allowed. Avoid giving write credentials to review-only agent runs.
acceptance_criteria: Design lists which actions are model-controlled vs executor-controlled, required preflight checks, token scoping, stale-head handling, protected labels, branch permissions, and forbidden defaults. It should explicitly keep auto-close/automerge out of default behavior.

title: Prototype opt-in bounded repair loop for PR review and CI fixes
description: Prototype an opt-in OpenHands repair loop for maintainer-triggered PR work: address review feedback, fix CI, or rebase. The loop should be bounded, observable, and exact-head gated. It should update a marker-backed status comment and stop with a clear blocked state when validation or permissions fail.
design: Start with @openhands fix ci / address review / rebase. Defer automerge. Preserve contributor credit in commits/PR body when replacing or repairing contributor work.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype or design covers trigger commands, max iterations, validation command selection, exact-head review/check gates, status updates, branch push policy, and blocked outcomes. It should not merge automatically unless a later explicit automerge design and repo-level opt-in exists.
